plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The minimal width $N_c(w)$ is determined by the algebraic rank of the constraint matrix formed by the $w$ sample points in a sufficiently rich feature space (e.g., via Fourier or polynomial basis), such that $N_c(w) \ge \text{rank}(\Phi)$, and rigidity is achieved when the feature map is injective on the constraint set.

steps.description: Implement a numerical experiment to test the hypothesis that minimal width $N_c(w)$ is determined by the algebraic rank of the constraint matrix $\Phi$ formed by $w$ sample points in a feature space. The workflow will: (1) generate synthetic constraints using a known function $f(x)$; (2) construct the feature matrix $\Phi$ using Fourier/polynomial basis; (3) compute rank($\Phi$); (4) train small feedforward networks of varying widths on $w$ points; (5) evaluate max absolute error on held-out points; (6) identify $N_c(w)$ as the smallest width achieving zero violation (error $\le 10^{-3}$); and (7) compare $N_c(w)$ to rank($\Phi$) to verify if rigidity is achieved when the feature map is injective. All results will be logged with convergence status and error metrics.
